item.title: Security
item.description:
Authentication Flow link

The admin-service acts as an OAuth2 Resource Server. It never issues tokens — it validates JWTs issued by Keycloak.

sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client (Postman / Service)
    participant KC as Keycloak :5433
    participant AD as Admin Service :8089

    C->>KC: POST /token (client_credentials)
    KC-->>C: JWT (realm_access.roles: ["ADMIN"])

    C->>AD: GET /api/admin/realm-roles + Bearer JWT
    AD->>AD: Validate JWT signature via JWK Set URI
    AD->>AD: Extract realm_access.roles → prefix ROLE_
    AD->>AD: @PreAuthorize → RolePermissionValidator
    AD->>AD: Lookup "query-realm" → ["ROLE_ADMIN"]
    AD->>AD: Compare with user authorities
    AD-->>C: 200 OK / 403 Forbidden

item.title: Keycloak Integration
item.description:
Overview link

The admin-service uses the Keycloak Admin Client (keycloak-admin-client:26.0.4) to programmatically manage the event-based-banking-service realm. It is the only service in the platform that holds admin-level Keycloak credentials.

The integration covers:

  • Creating confidential OAuth2 clients for new microservices (service accounts flow)
  • Listing and creating realm-level roles
  • Assigning roles to the service account of a newly provisioned client

KeyCloakManager link

KeyCloakManager is a @Component that acts as a factory and accessor for the Keycloak Admin API. It initialises the client on startup via @PostConstruct using the client_credentials grant type.
